A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same MPFT research. Their main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic-control experiments, K ablations, hardware measurements, and learning curves in Tables 1–2 and the main text and appendix figures.

after.justification: v2 reports original robotic-control, higher-dimensional, discrete-action, offline-data, sensitivity, and robustness results in Tables 1–3 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The four-stage MPFT procedure and network architectures remain substantially intact. v2 adds a one-hot adaptation of MOTD7 for discrete actions and corrects the stated PPO loss sign and GAE indexing. SPFT formalizes the single-track option already discussed in v1 Appendix C.2.

E1.justification: v2 removes Humanoid-2 while retaining the other six robotic tasks. It adds Lunar-Lander-4 and Fruit-Tree-6 with discrete actions, continuous Building-9, and pure offline evaluation on D4MORL MO-Hopper Expert and Amateur datasets. These substantially broaden objective dimensionality and data conditions.

E2.justification: C-MORL joins PGMORL and PA2D-MORL in the main robotic comparisons. New experiments also evaluate Envelope and GPI-LS in Table 3, and MORvS, CQL, and the behavioral policy in Table 18. These are reported comparators, not merely additional citations.

E3.justification: v2 adds expected utility evaluation using systematically sampled preferences. New protocols include a 100-hour timeout for higher-dimensional comparisons, a 1,500,000-step offline budget, and controlled variations of initialization, tracking, interaction budgets, and policy-buffer capacity. Retained robotic reward definitions and principal training settings are largely unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained K ablation and tracking analysis, Appendix G adds sensitivity to reverse/ascent scheduling and steps, robustness to initialization and tracking budgets, total interactions and policy-buffer size, and MPFT versus SPFT comparisons. The earlier CPU/memory study and SP convergence curves are removed.

E5.justification: Reported run counts change from three to five for the main results, K ablation, and convergence curves; mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting continues. Front visualizations are newly identified as best-seed plots. Table 18 reports five runs but supplies no dispersion estimates. These disclosures do not independently establish which experiments were rerun.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial EU, comparator, higher-dimensional, offline, and robustness results, while removing Humanoid and hardware results. Numerical revisions include Ant-2 MOTD7 HV changing from 7.144 to 7.04 million in Table 1, and HalfCheetah K=1 HV changing from 35.1 to 3.51 million in Table 2. Many other retained entries merely undergo rounding.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix C's regularized Lyapunov and switching-system analysis, assumptions, lemmas, discretization conditions, and claimed local exponential-convergence theorem. Appendix D replaces the earlier parallel-time calculation with serial training costs and policy-selection terms. Gradient and loss derivations also receive corrections.

C1.justification: v2 adds central claims of exponential convergence near the Pareto-stationary set and linear scaling with objective count. Performance claims now include expected utility and higher-dimensional tasks. The main contributions drop the earlier emphasis on hardware superiority and the claim to be the first continuous-action offline MP-MORL framework.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of disconnected-front coverage, reverse/ascent tradeoffs, and resource sensitivity. Appendix H discusses remaining coverage gaps, representation damage from reverse gradients, and the lack of universal curvature guarantees for nonconvex objectives. These materially expand applicability boundaries beyond v1's sparsity and resource tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 documents policy-buffer capacities, HV reference points, EU preference grids, C-MORL settings, higher-dimensional configurations, and offline sampling and budgets. Several are newly disclosed details rather than demonstrated changes to retained experiments. The reported code location changes from an anonymous repository to an author-named repository.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to Pareto-set learning, successor features, convex coverage sets, GPI-LS, and detailed C-MORL positioning, supplemented by Appendix E's comparison table. Relevant offline-learning and averaging references are added. C-MORL's underlying Liu et al. paper was already cited in v1; its comparative role is expanded.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, substantially rewrites the abstract and contributions, and refocuses Section 5 on TD7 while retaining PPO/SAC details in the appendix. Existing material is reorganized around separate notation, theory, metrics, comparisons, experiments, and limitations sections; network pseudocode moves to the end.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout, redraws Figure 1, and consolidates earlier main-text and appendix front plots into Figure 2. Table 1 gains EU rows and a C-MORL column. New visualization and analysis displays accompany removal of hardware plots, Humanoid panels, and SP learning curves.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical coverage, diagnostic analyses, and limitations compared with v1. However, its newly central convergence guarantee has a material proof gap: Appendix C.5 absorbs a Young-inequality remainder that need not vanish with mu into a C mu bound. New robustness prose also contradicts Table 16 by claiming unchanged Walker2d results across buffer sizes. The empirical gains coexist with reliability problems in important new claims, preventing a confident net-quality judgment.
